evaluations.evidence: view a list of sponsors
evaluations.rationale: Listing sponsors is self-contained and does not explicitly require another backlog story to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: view a list of user profiles
evaluations.rationale: Showing user profiles inherently requires user accounts/registration to exist; depends on the user registration story.

evaluations.evidence: email all the trainers at once from the website
evaluations.rationale: The story can be implemented as a standalone feature (collect trainer contacts) and does not explicitly reference another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: have a very clear map where the buildings and rooms are
evaluations.rationale: Providing a map is self-contained and does not inherently depend on any other story in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: trainer, I want to edit my training node myself
evaluations.rationale: Editing a trainer's training node is a standalone capability for trainers and does not explicitly require another story first.

evaluations.evidence: limit to one registration per day per authenticated user
evaluations.rationale: This constraint explicitly depends on the existence of authenticated user accounts / registration functionality.

evaluations.evidence: admin view that helps track registration status for each attendee
evaluations.rationale: Tracking registration status inherently requires a registration workflow and attendee registrations to exist (e.g., summit/training registration stories).

evaluations.evidence: be added to a training waitlist
evaluations.rationale: A waitlist requires a registration/registration-for-class feature (class must be registerable first).

evaluations.evidence: must accept the cancellation terms with a checkbox
evaluations.rationale: Accepting cancellation terms is part of the registration/cancellation workflow and thus depends on that registration flow being present for trainees.

evaluations.evidence: tie in a cancellation deadline to whatever registration / cancellation workflow exists
evaluations.rationale: This story explicitly references and depends on an existing registration/cancellation workflow elsewhere in the system.

evaluations.evidence: add to "my schedule" if there is a schedule feature on the site
evaluations.rationale: This story explicitly conditions itself on the existence of a schedule feature and therefore depends on that feature (schedule) being implemented.

evaluations.evidence: see which trainings I have signed up for
evaluations.rationale: Showing trainings a user signed up for requires a prior training signup/registration feature.

evaluations.evidence: view that is attached to their training node that shows all attendee information
evaluations.rationale: A trainer-facing attendee view requires attendee registration data for a training session to exist (i.e., registration functionality).

evaluations.evidence: admin view where all trainee information is shown and can be filtered to show a single training session
evaluations.rationale: Filtering trainee information by session presumes registrations/attendee records for sessions exist.

evaluations.evidence: dedicated page for each class ... link to register for class
evaluations.rationale: Creating a class detail page is a self-contained content/UI feature and does not inherently require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: training options clearly marked ... link to full details ... register now link
evaluations.rationale: Presenting training options is a standalone listing/detail feature and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: training landing page with an intro section and a list of all training offerings
evaluations.rationale: A landing/listing page for training offerings is self-contained and does not require other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: have a link on the home page to a list of training options
evaluations.rationale: Adding a navigation link is self-contained and does not inherently depend on other stories.

evaluations.evidence: find out where the coding lounge is and what time it is open
evaluations.rationale: Providing location/time info is self-contained content and does not require another story first.

evaluations.evidence: refund sponsorship money that was processed via stripe
evaluations.rationale: Refunding money presumes payment processing and captured transactions exist (payment/charging story).

evaluations.evidence: find a link on the sponsorships page to become a $350 level sponsor
evaluations.rationale: Adding a link to a sponsorship option is a UI/content task and can be implemented independently.

evaluations.evidence: See a list of attendees associated with this company
evaluations.rationale: Listing attendees associated with a company requires attendee–sponsor linkage or data about attendees tied to sponsors (a sponsor-linking feature).

evaluations.evidence: identify myself as and pay for a $350 company sponsorship
evaluations.rationale: Paying for a sponsorship requires the payment/charging flow to be implemented.

evaluations.evidence: create and maintain venues
evaluations.rationale: Venue CRUD is a standalone administrative feature and does not inherently depend on other stories.

evaluations.evidence: view venue details
evaluations.rationale: Viewing venue details requires venues to be created/maintained first.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of the sessions associated with sponsor attendees
evaluations.rationale: Showing sessions associated with sponsor attendees presumes sponsors are assigned to sessions/events via an assignment feature.

evaluations.evidence: See a payment page to pay for my individual sponsorships as the third step of the registration process
evaluations.rationale: A payment page as part of registration depends on the payment/charging functionality being available.

evaluations.evidence: assign sponsors to events, trainings and summits
evaluations.rationale: Assigning sponsors presumes that sponsor entities exist (sponsorship purchase/creation) to be assigned to events.

evaluations.evidence: see all events, trainings and summits that a sponsor is sponsoring
evaluations.rationale: Displaying the events a sponsor is sponsoring depends on sponsors being assigned to those events (assignment feature).

evaluations.evidence: Enter payment information and have my card charged for an individual sponsorship
evaluations.rationale: Payment/charging is a self-contained feature and can be implemented independently.

evaluations.evidence: link BADCamp attendees to my sponsorship page
evaluations.rationale: Allowing a sponsor to link attendees to their sponsorship page can be implemented as a self-contained action for sponsors.

evaluations.evidence: update my user profile
evaluations.rationale: Profile update is a typical self-contained user feature that does not inherently depend on other stories.

evaluations.evidence: sign up for the BADCamp newsletter
evaluations.rationale: Newsletter signup is a standalone feature and does not require another backlog story first.

evaluations.evidence: tag my blog posts for consumption by Drupal Planet
evaluations.rationale: Tagging blog posts presumes blog posts exist and can be created/edited (blog post creation story).

evaluations.evidence: create blog posts
evaluations.rationale: Creating blog posts is a content creation capability and does not inherently require another story.

evaluations.evidence: read the blog
evaluations.rationale: Reading the blog requires blog content to exist (blog post creation).

evaluations.evidence: sponsor a summit that matches my brand
evaluations.rationale: Sponsoring a summit implies a sponsorship purchase mechanism exists (payment/sponsorship creation).

evaluations.evidence: register for a summit
evaluations.rationale: Registering requires that the summit exists/listed (summit creation/listing by coordinator).

evaluations.evidence: get detailed directions to the summit venue
evaluations.rationale: Providing directions depends on venue data being available (venue creation/maintenance).

evaluations.evidence: see what summits I'm signed up for
evaluations.rationale: Showing summits the user is signed up for requires summit registration records to exist.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of attendees signed up for my summit
evaluations.rationale: A coordinator's attendee list presumes attendees have registered for that summit.

evaluations.evidence: list basic information about my summit
evaluations.rationale: Providing basic summit information is a content/management task that can be implemented independently.

evaluations.evidence: list sponsors for my summit
evaluations.rationale: Listing sponsors for a summit depends on sponsors being assigned to that summit (assignment feature).

evaluations.evidence: list an agenda for my summit
evaluations.rationale: Creating an agenda is a standalone content feature for the coordinator and does not require another backlog story first.

evaluations.evidence: see how many seats are left for the summit
evaluations.rationale: Reporting remaining seats requires a registration/capacity mechanism and registration records to exist.

evaluations.evidence: see specific details on summits
evaluations.rationale: A summit detail page is a self-contained content/view feature and does not inherently require another story.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of all the summits
evaluations.rationale: Listing summits is a standalone listing feature and can be implemented without requiring another specific story first.

evaluations.evidence: learn about sponsorship levels
evaluations.rationale: Providing sponsorship level information is content that can be implemented independently.

evaluations.evidence: use a WYSIWYG editor for all long-form content
evaluations.rationale: Providing a WYSIWYG editing capability is a standalone feature for authenticated users and does not inherently require another story.

evaluations.evidence: Link to my sponsorship profile from my job listings
evaluations.rationale: Linking from job listings to sponsorship profiles presumes job listings exist (job posting functionality).

evaluations.evidence: learn about posting jobs as a sponsor and contact the sponsorship person
evaluations.rationale: Providing information about posting jobs and contact details is a self-contained content piece.

evaluations.evidence: post a job
evaluations.rationale: Posting a job is a content posting feature and can be implemented independently.

evaluations.evidence: view the job board
evaluations.rationale: Viewing the job board is meaningful only if job postings exist; it depends on job posting functionality.

evaluations.evidence: assign a room to a time slot and a location, so that I can populate the schedule
evaluations.rationale: Assigning rooms/time slots presumes sessions exist and (often) that sessions have been accepted; it depends on session acceptance/approval features.

evaluations.evidence: see the schedule
evaluations.rationale: Viewing the schedule is a presentation feature and can be implemented independently (even if empty initially).

evaluations.evidence: see the final list of sessions approved
evaluations.rationale: A final list of approved sessions requires an approval workflow (bulk or single acceptance) to have been performed.

evaluations.evidence: bulk approve sessions as accepted
evaluations.rationale: Bulk approving presumes sessions have been submitted (session submission stories).

evaluations.evidence: mark a session as accepted
evaluations.rationale: Marking acceptance requires a session to exist (session submission) to be accepted.

evaluations.evidence: receive a notification when sessions have been evaluated
evaluations.rationale: Notifications on evaluation depend on the session evaluation/acceptance mechanism and on session submissions existing.

evaluations.evidence: receive a notification when I submit a session
evaluations.rationale: Receiving a notification on submission depends on the session submission feature being implemented.

evaluations.evidence: edit my session
evaluations.rationale: Editing a session presumes a session submission exists to be edited.

evaluations.evidence: register to speak at BADCamp, so that I submit a session
evaluations.rationale: Submitting/registering to speak is a self-contained action to create a session submission and does not depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: submit a session at BADCAMP
evaluations.rationale: Session submission is a standalone feature that creates the session entities used by other stories.

evaluations.evidence: personalize my sponsorship page
evaluations.rationale: Personalizing a sponsor page assumes the sponsor account/page exists, which depends on sponsorship creation/purchase.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of all the summits that include when they are
evaluations.rationale: Listing summits with dates is a content/listing feature and can be implemented independently.

evaluations.rationale: Offering sponsorship choices during registration presumes a multi-step registration/payment process and a payment page exists.

evaluations.evidence: find a link in the menu that links to the registration form
evaluations.rationale: A menu link to a registration form depends on that registration form existing (user registration).

evaluations.evidence: fill out a user registration form
evaluations.rationale: User registration form is a self-contained feature and does not inherently depend on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: find session information
evaluations.rationale: Providing access to session information is a standalone retrieval/display feature and does not necessarily depend on other stories.
